types.name: Fiber
types.doc: A fiber is a stackful coroutine: a function call that runs on its own stack and can be suspended at any call depth with `suspend`. It is created with `fiber f(args)` and advanced with `resume`. A fiber carries no value. Use a generator to produce values.

methods.name: cancel
methods.doc: Ends a fiber that is not done without running the rest of its function. Every call that the fiber is in returns at once, from the innermost one out, and the values that the calls own are destructed as at a `return`. A fiber that was never resumed is ended without the call and its arguments are released. A `@deinit` that the unwinding calls runs, and when it stops at a `suspend` or an `await` it ends there the same way. Returns whether the fiber is done afterwards. A fiber that is running is not cancelled.

methods.name: resume
methods.doc: Runs the fiber until it suspends or its function returns. Returns `.suspended` or `.done`. Resuming a fiber that is done returns `.done`.

methods.name: waiting
methods.doc: Whether the fiber is suspended at an `await` or a `Future.wait_any` whose future is not done, or in a `Fiber.wait_ready` while none of its own fibers can go on. A `resume` of such a fiber returns `.suspended` at once.

funcs.name: wait_ready
funcs.doc: Waits until a future that a suspended fiber of this thread awaits is done, and returns `true`. Returns `false` at once when no fiber awaits a future. A scheduler loop calls it when a round of `resume` calls made no progress. Futures of spawned threads are waited for like `await` does. When only the host can complete the futures, the eval is suspended and all of them are pending (see `cl_vm_pending_futures`). Inside a fiber, that fiber is suspended until a future is done that one of its own fibers awaits: a fiber that it resumed last or asked `waiting()` about last, or a fiber of one of those. It returns `false` at once when none of them awaits a future.

types.name: Scope
types.doc: A group of fibers that do not outlive it. `start` adds a fiber and `join` runs the fibers until all of them are done. A scope that is destructed joins its fibers first, so a fiber of a scope never runs after the block that holds the scope. The entry function of a fiber returns `void` or `!void`. `join` returns the first error that a fiber returned. After an error the other fibers are cancelled (`Fiber.cancel`): they do not run on.

methods.name: start

methods.name: active

methods.name: join
methods.doc: Runs the fibers until all of them are done. A fiber that stops at `suspend` gives the others a turn. When every fiber waits for a future, the scope waits like `Fiber.wait_ready`. Returns the first error that a fiber returned. More fibers can be started after a `join`.

methods.name: abort
methods.doc: Cancels the fibers that are not done (`Fiber.cancel`) and drops an error that a fiber returned. A fiber that can not be cancelled runs to its end first.

Offset: `%z` (`+0900`), `%:z` (`+09:00`), `%Z` (the abbreviation of the zone such as `KST`, or `UTC`, or the offset when the value has no zone). Others: `%F` (`%Y-%m-%d`), `%T` (`%H:%M:%S`), `%R` (`%H:%M`), `%D` (`%m/%d/%y`), `%s` (Unix seconds), `%n`, `%t`, `%%`. Names are in English. `error.Format` for another specifier.

types.name: Disambiguation

funcs.name: new_slice_buffer
funcs.doc: A `Slice` buffer holds the number of initialized elements in its first 8 bytes, then the elements. Slices that share a buffer can have different lengths, so `Slice.@deinit` destructs this count instead of its own length. Ops that resize keep it equal to the result's length. A `Slice` that owns its buffer (`owns_buffer`) is never a sub-slice, so its count is `(as[Ptr[int]] ptr)[-1]` (no call, hot path). Only managed element types read the count, so the resize ops skip it for the others.

funcs.doc: Change the current working directory.

funcs.name: exec
funcs.doc: Runs a shell command and returns the stdout/stderr.

funcs.name: exit
funcs.doc: Exits the program with a status code.

funcs.name: fetch_url
funcs.doc: Fetches the contents at `url` using the HTTP GET request method.

funcs.name: file_exists
funcs.doc: Checks whether the file at the given `path` exists.

funcs.name: free
funcs.doc: Frees the memory located at `ptr`.

funcs.name: last_error
funcs.doc: The error of the last failed OS call, from `errno` (POSIX) or `GetLastError` (Windows). Read it right after the call: a later call can change it. `last_os_error` gives the code itself.

funcs.name: last_os_error
funcs.doc: The code of the last failed OS call: `errno` (POSIX) or `GetLastError` (Windows).

funcs.name: from_win32_error
funcs.doc: Converts a Windows error code (`GetLastError`) to the standard error name. See `from_errno`. Off Windows it gives `error.Unknown`.

funcs.name: from_errno
funcs.doc: Converts an `errno` code to the standard error name. Codes without a name give `error.Unknown`, and so does every code on Windows. The names are the same on every platform (`from_win32_error` for Windows codes): `NotFound`, `PermissionDenied`, `AlreadyExists`, `NotADirectory`, `IsADirectory`, `DirectoryNotEmpty`, `NoSpace`, `ReadOnly`, `NameTooLong`, `TooManyOpenFiles`, `Busy`, `CrossesDevices`, `Interrupted`, `WouldBlock`, `TimedOut`, `BrokenPipe`, `ConnectionRefused`, `OutOfMemory`, `InvalidArgument`, `Unsupported`, `Unknown`.

funcs.name: get_env
funcs.doc: Returns an environment variable by key.

funcs.name: get_env_all
funcs.doc: Returns all environment variables as a map.

funcs.name: malloc
funcs.doc: Allocates `size` bytes of memory and returns a pointer.

funcs.name: num_cpus
funcs.doc: Returns the number of CPU cores on the current machine.

funcs.name: open_dir
funcs.doc: Opens a directory at the given `path`. `iterable` indicates that the directory's entries can be iterated.

funcs.name: nano_time
funcs.doc: Returns the current time in nanoseconds since the Epoch.

funcs.name: now
funcs.doc: High resolution timestamp. Returns a relative up-time in nanoseconds.

funcs.name: open_file
funcs.doc: Opens a file at the given `path` with an `OpenMode`.

funcs.name: parse_args
funcs.doc: Returns a result that can be used to query args. `opts`: The name of options to match excluding the hyphen prefix. eg. `-path`

funcs.name: read_file
funcs.doc: Reads the file at `path` as text. Returns `error.Unicode` when the contents are not valid UTF-8. Read bytes with `read_file_bytes`.

funcs.name: read_file_bytes
funcs.doc: Reads the file contents from `path` as bytes.

funcs.name: remove_dir
funcs.doc: Removes an empty directory at `path`.

funcs.name: remove_file
funcs.doc: Removes the file at `path`.

funcs.name: resolve_exe_path
funcs.doc: Returns the current executable's path.

funcs.name: resolve_path
funcs.doc: Returns the absolute path of the given path.

funcs.name: set_env
funcs.doc: Sets an environment variable by key.

funcs.name: sleep
funcs.doc: Pauses the current thread for `nsecs` nanoseconds.

funcs.name: unset_env
funcs.doc: Removes an environment variable by key.

funcs.name: write_file
funcs.doc: Writes the text `contents` to a file. Write bytes with `write_file_bytes`.

funcs.name: write_file_bytes
funcs.doc: Writes the bytes `contents` to a file.

funcs.name: open_lib
funcs.doc: Creates a handle to a dynamic library.

funcs.name: compile
funcs.doc: Compiles a grammar. Returns `error.Syntax` for a grammar that is malformed, calls a rule that is not defined, is left recursive or repeats something that can match nothing, and `error.TooBig` for one that is over `MaxInsts`.

funcs.name: compile
funcs.doc: Compiles a grammar. On failure, `diag` tells where and why.

funcs.name: unicode_version
funcs.doc: Returns the version of the Unicode Character Database that the classes come from, such as `18.0.0`.

funcs.name: compile
funcs.doc: Compiles a pattern. Returns `error.Syntax` for a pattern that is malformed or uses a feature that is not supported, and `error.TooBig` for one that is over `MaxInsts`.

funcs.name: compile
funcs.doc: Compiles a pattern. On failure, `diag` tells where and why.

funcs.name: escape
funcs.doc: Returns `s` with every character that has a meaning in a pattern escaped, so that it matches itself.

funcs.name: is_leap_year
funcs.doc: Whether `year` has 366 days.

funcs.name: days_in_month
funcs.doc: Returns the number of days of `month` (1 to 12) in `year`.

funcs.name: nanos
funcs.doc: Returns a duration of `n` nanoseconds.

funcs.name: days
funcs.doc: Returns a duration of `n` times 24 hours.

funcs.name: now
funcs.doc: Returns the current time of the system clock. The clock can be set, so it can go back: measure elapsed time with `monotonic`.

funcs.name: monotonic
funcs.doc: Returns the reading of a clock that never goes back. Only the difference of two readings has a meaning.

funcs.name: unix
funcs.doc: Returns the instant `sec` seconds after 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, or before it when `sec` is negative.

funcs.name: unix
funcs.doc: `nsec` can be any number of nanoseconds. It is added to `sec`.

funcs.name: datetime
funcs.sig: datetime(year int, month int, day int, hour int, minute int, second int) -> !DateTime
funcs.doc: Returns a date and time of day in UTC. `error.Range` when a field is out of range or the day does not exist.

funcs.name: datetime
funcs.sig: datetime(year int, month int, day int, hour int, minute int, second int, nsec int, offset int) -> !DateTime
funcs.doc: Returns a date and time of day at `offset` minutes east of UTC.

funcs.name: date
funcs.sig: date(year int, month int, day int) -> !Date
funcs.doc: Returns a calendar day. `error.Range` when the day does not exist, such as February 30.

funcs.name: parse
funcs.doc: Parses an RFC 3339 timestamp such as `2026-11-15T10:22:03.5+09:00`. The text must have a UTC offset. A space can stand for the `T`, `,` for the `.`, and the offset can be `Z`, `+09:00`, `+0900` or `+09`. `error.Syntax` when the text has another shape, `error.Range` when a field is out of range.

funcs.name: parse
funcs.doc: On failure, `diag` tells where and why.

funcs.name: parse
funcs.doc: Parses a timestamp that can be without a UTC offset, such as `2026-11-15 10:22:03`: it is read at `offset` minutes east of UTC. An offset in the text wins.

funcs.name: parse_format
funcs.doc: Parses `s` by a `strptime` format, such as `%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z`. The specifiers are those of `DateTime.format` without `%u %w %G %V`. A number takes one or two digits (`%Y` four, `%f` one to nine), a space in the format takes one or more, `%b` and `%a` take the short or the full name in any case, and `%z` takes `Z`, `+0900`, `+09:00` or `+09`. A field that the format does not have is that of 1970-01-01T00:00:00, and without `%z` the text is read as UTC. `error.Syntax` when the text does not fit, `error.Range` for a field out of range and `error.Format` for a specifier that is not known.

funcs.name: parse_format
funcs.sig: parse_format(s str, fmt str, offset int) -> !DateTime
funcs.doc: A text without `%z` is read at `offset` minutes east of UTC.

funcs.name: parse_format
funcs.sig: parse_format(s str, fmt str, offset int, diag &&Diag) -> !DateTime

funcs.name: parse_date
funcs.doc: Parses a date such as `2026-11-15`.

funcs.name: parse_offset
funcs.doc: Parses a UTC offset such as `+05:30`, `-0330`, `+09` or `Z` and returns the minutes east of UTC.

funcs.name: format_offset
funcs.doc: Returns an offset in minutes as `+05:30`. Panics when the offset is out of range.

funcs.name: zone
funcs.doc: Returns the time zone of an IANA name such as `Asia/Seoul` or `America/New_York`, read from the time zone database of the system: the directory in `TZDIR`, then `/usr/share/zoneinfo` and the like. `UTC` is always there. `error.NotFound` when the system has no zone by that name, or no database (Windows, wasm): give the data with `zone_from_tzif` there.

funcs.name: local
funcs.doc: Returns the time zone of the system: what `TZ` says (a zone name, the path of a TZif file or a POSIX rule), or else `/etc/localtime`. `error.NotFound` when the system does not say, or says something that can not be read.

funcs.name: zone_from_tzif
funcs.doc: Returns the time zone of a TZif file (RFC 9636), the format of the files in a zoneinfo directory. `error.Syntax` when the data is not a TZif file.

funcs.name: zone_from_posix
funcs.doc: Returns the time zone of a POSIX `TZ` rule such as `KST-9` or `EST5EDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0`. The offset in a rule is positive west of UTC.

funcs.name: parse_zoned
funcs.doc: Parses an RFC 9557 timestamp: RFC 3339 with a time zone in brackets, such as `2026-07-04T08:00:00-04:00[America/New_York]`. The zone is read with `time.zone`, and the value is in it. The offset says which of two readings it is when the clock was set back. With `Z` in the place of the offset, or without one, the zone gives the offset. A text without brackets is read as `time.parse` reads it, and `[+09:00]` is a fixed offset. Other tags in brackets such as `[u-ca=gregory]` are skipped. `error.NotFound` when the system does not have the zone, and `error.Conflict` when the offset in the text is not the offset of the zone at that time: the rules of the zone changed after the text was written.

funcs.name: assert
funcs.doc: Panics if `pred` is `false`.

funcs.name: eq
funcs.doc: Returns whether two values are equal. Panics with `error.AssertError` if types or values do not match up.

funcs.name: eq_slice
funcs.doc: This will be deprecated once `eq_span` can accept `AsSpan[%T]`.

funcs.name: eq_span
funcs.doc: Returns `true` if two spans have the same size and the elements are equal as if `eq` was called on those corresponding elements.

funcs.name: eq_near
funcs.sig: eq_near(exp float, act float, epsilon float)

funcs.name: encode
funcs.doc: Encodes a value as TOON text. Returns `error.Unicode` when a string or key is not valid UTF-8.

funcs.name: decode
funcs.doc: Decodes TOON text. Returns `error.Syntax` for malformed input and `error.Unicode` for input that is not UTF-8.

funcs.name: decode
funcs.doc: Decodes TOON text. On failure, `diag` tells where and why.

funcs.name: from_json
funcs.doc: Converts JSON text to TOON text.

funcs.name: to_json
funcs.doc: Converts TOON text to compact JSON text.

funcs.name: join
funcs.doc: Joins two paths with `/` and normalizes the result. An empty part is skipped, and a part that starts with `/` does not drop the parts before it: `join('a', '/b')` is `'a/b'`. Joining only empty parts gives `''`.

funcs.name: join
funcs.doc: Joins the parts with `/` and normalizes the result, like `join(a, b)`.

funcs.name: normalize
funcs.doc: Returns the shortest path that names the same place, by reading the string only: it removes empty and `.` parts, removes a `..` together with the part before it, and removes a trailing `/`. A `..` at the start of a relative path stays, and a `..` right after the root is removed (`'/..'` is `'/'`). An empty path gives `'.'`.

funcs.name: base
funcs.doc: Returns the last part of the path. Trailing `/` are ignored: `base('a/b/')` is `'b'`. `base('/')` is `'/'` and `base('')` is `'.'`.

funcs.name: dir
funcs.doc: Returns the path without its last part, normalized. Trailing `/` are ignored: `dir('a/b/')` is `'a'`. A path with no `/` gives `'.'`, and `dir('/a')` and `dir('/')` give `'/'`.

funcs.name: ext
funcs.doc: Returns the extension of the last part, from its last `.`: `ext('a/b.tar.gz')` is `'.gz'`. A name without a `.` and a name that only starts with one (`'.bashrc'`) give `''`.

funcs.name: stem
funcs.doc: Returns the last part without its extension: `stem('a/b.tar.gz')` is `'b.tar'`, `stem('.bashrc')` is `'.bashrc'`.
